definitions.explanation: A person who rides a horse, especially a professional jockey in horse racing. Can also refer more broadly to any mounted rider.

examples.japanese: {騎手|きしゅ}が{馬|うま}に{乗|の}る。
{若|わか}い{騎手|きしゅ}が{初|はつ}{勝利|しょうり}を{挙|あ}げた。
examples.english: The young jockey achieved his first victory.

examples.japanese: {競馬|けいば}では{馬|うま}の{能力|のうりょく}だけでなく、{騎手|きしゅ}の{腕前|うでまえ}も{勝敗|しょうはい}を{大|おお}きく{左右|さゆう}する。
examples.english: In horse racing, not only the horse's ability but also the jockey's skill greatly influences the outcome.

notes:
A compound of {騎|き} (riding, mounted) and {手|しゅ} (person, hand). In modern usage, primarily refers to professional jockeys in {競馬|けいば} (horse racing). Japan has a well-established horse racing industry (JRA — Japan Racing Association), and famous jockeys are widely known public figures.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {騎手|きしゅ}になる: to become a jockey
- {騎手|きしゅ}が{騎乗|きじょう}する: a jockey rides (formal)
- {騎手|きしゅ}の{腕前|うでまえ}: the jockey's skill
- リーディング{騎手|きしゅ}: leading jockey (most wins in a season)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ジョッキー: jockey — the loanword, used interchangeably in casual contexts
- {騎馬|きば}: mounted warrior, horseman — historical or military term
- {乗|の}り{手|て}: rider — more general term for anyone who rides (horses, motorcycles, etc.)
